onboarding_empty_description: Publish your first blueprint to share a proven code pattern with the team. You can do it right from the web, or push from the terminal with the CLI.
onboarding_empty_cli_hint: Or from the terminal: blueprint push
device_description: Enter the code displayed in your terminal to connect this device to your account.
device_approved: Device authorized! You can close this page and go back to your terminal.
device_error: Invalid or expired code. Check the code in your terminal and try again.
device_login_required: Sign in with Google to authorize this device.
onboarding_welcome_description: Discover proven code patterns shared by the team. Search in natural language, then pull them straight into your codebase.
cli_intro: Publish and pull blueprints straight from your terminal with the theodo-blueprints CLI.
cli_install_description: Run the quick install script for your platform. To update later, run theodo-blueprints update (the CLI also tells you once a day when a newer release exists).
cli_auth_description: Log in with the device flow, or generate a token from your account and pass it directly.
cli_auth_token_hint: Prefer a token? Generate one from your account and pass it to
cli_usage_description: Each command with a copy-ready example.
cli_cmd_list: List blueprints, optionally filtered by stack or tag
cli_cmd_pull: Download a blueprint to a local markdown file
cli_cmd_push: Publish a blueprint markdown file, optionally under a project
cli_cmd_sync: Publish a whole @Blueprint catalog from its TSV index (see below)
cli_cmd_projects: List the projects you can publish to, or join one
cli_cmd_update: Update the CLI to the latest release (add --check to only look)
cli_sync_description: If your repo uses the blueprint skill (@Blueprint annotations), publish its whole catalog in one command. Each @Blueprint becomes a registry blueprint whose slug is its pattern id, so re-running sync updates in place and never duplicates.
layer_database_description: Schemas, migrations, repositories and data access
layer_api_description: Routes, controllers, middleware and request validation
layer_domain_description: Business rules, services and pure core logic
layer_state_description: Client state, data fetching and caching
layer_infra_description: Deployment, containers, CI and cloud resources
layer_testing_description: Test setups, fixtures and testing patterns
layer_tooling_description: Build, lint, code generation and developer tooling
stacks_intro: Named technology presets. A stack gathers every blueprint carrying one of its technologies, layer by layer, ready to scaffold into a new project.
stack_form_hint: The stack will gather every blueprint carrying at least one of these technologies.
stack_scaffold_hint: Writes one markdown file per blueprint, grouped by layer, with an index.md to start from.
stack_blueprints_empty: No blueprint uses these technologies yet
stack_confirm_delete: Delete the stack "{name}"? Its blueprints are kept.
